title: Research authorized fulfillment options and record the Instacart Developer Platform decision
body:
## Role
A senior product engineer doing a bounded research spike, with legal review where needed.

## Goal
Decide build, partner or avoid for the Instacart Developer Platform as the first authorized fulfillment adapter, and score the other authorized options (backlog P2.2) so the choice is comparative, not assumed.

## Context
ADR 0001 retired the private Safeway API; no adapter is built from undocumented endpoints. Instacart's public Developer Platform documents a shopping-list link endpoint ([docs](https://docs.instacart.com/developer_platform_api/api/products/create_shopping_list_page)). The epic (#142) summarizes what those pages verify and what they leave out. Open questions the pages don't answer:
- program eligibility and the Developer Terms (linked from the docs, not yet read)
- how a production key is issued (the overview says "contact your representative", the API-keys page describes self-service)
- what happens when a link expires, and whether affiliate parameters in the response carry attribution obligations
- data rights: what Instacart may do with the item names and filters we send
- the supported units list (an unsupported unit makes quantity matching fail)
- rate limits (429 is documented, no number)
- whether the Nearby Retailers API or recipe pages change the design

## Deliverables
1. `docs/research/fulfillment-options.md`: a scored comparison (reach, approval likelihood, economics, data rights, checkout support, maintenance, lock-in) covering Instacart, retailer affiliate or deep-link programs, and receipt/order import options.
2. ADR 0002 recording the decision, the adapter capability Instacart actually supports, and any terms constraints the code must honor.
3. A short list of follow-up changes to the child issues of the epic, if the findings change them.

## Concrete examples
- If the terms forbid caching links or sending dietary filters, the ADR says so and #147/#148 are amended before work starts.
- If a production key needs a partnership, the ADR records "development key for dogfood only" and the epic's done-when changes.

## Constraints
- Research only: no adapter code, no API calls with a real key in this issue.
- Cite the official page for every provider fact.
- Never paste a key into the repo, an issue or a doc.

## Dependencies
None. Can start now, in parallel with Milestone B core work.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0002 merged with a build/partner/avoid decision and the capability name the adapter may claim.
- [ ] Every open question above is answered or marked unknown with who can answer it.
- [ ] #140 decision 5 (fulfillment path) is ticked or explicitly deferred.

## Testing requirements
Docs-only. `./scripts/check-all.sh` still passes.

## Out of scope
Implementing the adapter, browser assistance (P2.1), receipt import.

## Documentation requirements
ADR 0002, `docs/adr/README.md` index, backlog P2.2 and P1.11 updated to the verified decision.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
